title: File upload does not honor its AbortSignal
verification: Actual native FileBackend reproducer repeated three times before and after the fix; two regression failures before, five passing cases after.
evidence: Method accepts signal but pipeline and staging do not use it; S3 upload explicitly handles cancellation.
experiment: Call the actual FileBackend with an already-aborted signal, then cancel an in-flight body; check promise outcome, source lifecycle, published bytes and staging cleanup.
confirm: Aborted transfers are reported successful or continue waiting for a body despite cancellation.
refute: Existing layers cancel the actual operation and the contract intentionally excludes adapter cancellation.
impact: Cancelled adapter calls continue and report success. Endpoint and production impact remain unverified.
verificationCost: Low: existing temporary-file unit setup; no external services.
stopCondition: Do not submit if intentional or already covered by active upstream implementation.

title: File downloads ignore caller cancellation
evidence: Shared signature accepts a signal; file implementation stops at headers.
experiment: Cancel a pending local read or MD5 calculation; inspect file streams and consumer behavior.
impact: Possible unnecessary disk I/O for cancelled local downloads; HTTP streaming may already destroy the body.
stopCondition: Reject claims based only on a missing positional parameter; prove a real lifecycle failure.

title: File copy may publish bytes before metadata succeeds
evidence: copyFile precedes metadata persistence. However, ObjectStorage uses a fresh version, so direct backend overwrite is not proof of production corruption.
experiment: Inject a metadata failure and trace the real version publication and cleanup path.
impact: Unknown; avoid claiming published-object corruption without testing higher layers.
stopCondition: Drop if version indirection and existing cleanup make this a harmless temporary state.

title: S3 and TUS lock protocol gaps from earlier advice
evidence: Open targeted fixes already cover stale leases, overlapping renewals, metadata header collisions and conditional HEAD.
stopCondition: No competing implementation; only revisit with a demonstrably missing independent case.

title: Benchmark large-bucket listing before selecting a bottleneck
evidence: No local performance baseline or proven bottleneck yet.
experiment: Only after functional setup, define representative data and repeated measurements.
stopCondition: Do not build a benchmark platform without a concrete question and resource budget.
